identity.title: RealPDEBench: A Benchmark for Complex Physical Systems with Real-World Data

problem.claim: Predicting the evolution of complex physical systems is a central scientific and engineering task.

gap.claim: Scientific ML largely relies on simulated data because expensive real-world measurements are scarce, limiting evaluation and sim-to-real research.

contributions.claim: Introduces RealPDEBench, integrating real-world measurements with paired numerical simulations.
Provides five datasets, three tasks, nine metrics, and ten baselines spanning complex physical systems.
Reports discrepancies between simulated and real-world data and evaluates methods for bridging them.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe RealPDEBench as the first scientific-ML benchmark integrating real-world measurements with paired simulations.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Authors report significant discrepancies between simulated and real-world data.
Authors report that simulated-data pretraining consistently improves accuracy and convergence.
Authors report benchmarking ten representative baselines, including state-of-the-art models, pretrained PDE foundation models, and a traditional method.

narrative_sequence.summary: Complex-system evolution prediction is important, but scientific ML is constrained by scarce real-world data and dependence on simulations.
This data gap limits model development, evaluation, and sim-to-real research.
The paper presents RealPDEBench with paired measured and simulated datasets across five physical-system datasets.

It defines three comparison or bridging tasks, nine data- and physics-oriented metrics, and ten baselines; experiments report simulation–reality discrepancies and benefits from simulated-data pretraining.

source_observation.claim: The benchmark pairs real measurements with simulations and evaluates them using both data-oriented and physics-oriented metrics.

lessons.interpretation: Pairing domains and measuring both predictive fit and physical behavior can expose mismatches that a single metric may hide.
lessons.application: For a scientific-ML study, construct paired real/simulated splits and report separate data-fit and physics-consistency metrics.
lessons.exception: This is unsuitable when real measurements cannot be paired or when the application has no meaningful physics-based evaluation criterion.

source_observation.claim: The authors explicitly report simulation–reality discrepancies before reporting consistent gains from simulated-data pretraining.

lessons.interpretation: Separating domain mismatch from transfer gains makes the claim about pretraining more informative.
lessons.application: Present baseline domain discrepancies first, then quantify how pretraining changes accuracy and convergence under the same evaluation setup.
lessons.exception: Avoid this framing when no comparable real-world evaluation data exist.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify dataset domains, sizes, task definitions, metric formulas, baseline configurations, or numerical effect sizes.
The reported pretraining improvements lack detailed conditions and statistical or reproducibility information in the supplied units.
